title: The Kannada Poet
philosophicalAnchor: The wise courtier remembers only what matters most—the recent poems. When memory fills, the least recently used verse is forgotten. This is the elegant compromise of caching: trade completeness for speed.
pythonConcept: LRU cache, OrderedDict, collections.OrderedDict, cache eviction, memoization
briefDescription: Implement an LRU cache for the Vijayanagara court poet using OrderedDict, remembering only the 3 most recently requested poems.
theoryPillar: LRU (Least Recently Used) caching keeps frequently accessed items in memory while evicting the least recently accessed ones when capacity is reached. Cache hits return instantly; cache misses incur full computation.
anchorPillar: The poet takes 2 seconds per verse. The courtier can only remember 3 poems. Cache hits return instantly. When memory is full and a new poem is needed, the one not recited for the longest time is forgotten.
triggerPillar: Couriers ask for poems repeatedly. Remembering all poems is impossible. The system must balance memory constraints with the reality that recently requested poems are more likely to be requested again.
realityPillar: collections.OrderedDict remembers insertion order. cache.move_to_end() marks an item as recently used. cache.popitem(last=False) removes the oldest item. Capacity checking and conditional adding implement the full LRU policy.
